prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
It’s time for real change. Labour will rebuild a fair, green, democratic Britain that works for the many, not the few—taking on vested interests, reversing austerity and sharing wealth and power.

A Green Industrial Revolution
- Invest £400bn (including a £250bn Green Transformation Fund) via a National Investment Bank and regional banks to decarbonise the economy, raise living standards and create one million good, unionised jobs.
- Deliver 90% clean electricity by 2030; ban fracking; roll out offshore/onshore wind, solar, tidal, storage and district heat; upgrade almost all homes to high-efficiency standards; cut fuel poverty; support workers in transition; windfall tax on oil companies.
- Bring energy and water into democratic public ownership to prioritise sustainability, end profiteering and accelerate grid upgrades. Expand community energy.

Rewiring the economy and levelling up
- Decentralise power, put investment and decision-making in every region; shift Treasury functions north; use procurement to boost UK supply chains, trade union rights and equalities.
- Back industry and innovation: 3% of GDP for R&D, green steel and plastics remanufacturing, gigafactories, reshoring, export a high-standards “green made in Britain.”

Public services and fair taxation
- Rebuild services by asking the top 5% and big corporations to pay more, cracking down on avoidance, and guaranteeing no VAT rise.
- End outsourcing and PFI; presumption to insource; £150bn Social Transformation Fund to renew schools, hospitals, care homes and council housing; restore public sector pay.

NHS and care
- End privatisation; 4.3% average annual health spending rise; expand mental health with parity of esteem; free prescriptions and basic dentistry; protect NHS data.
- Create a National Care Service with free personal care, ethical provision, better pay and training for care workers, and higher Carer’s Allowance.

Education for all
- A cradle‑to‑grave National Education Service: restore Sure Start (Sure Start Plus), 30 hours free preschool for 2–4-year-olds, more staff and fair pay.
- Properly fund schools; cap primary classes at 30; scrap high-stakes SATs; Arts Premium; bring academies/free schools under local democratic oversight; free school meals for all primary pupils.
- Lifelong learning entitlements; abolish tuition fees and restore maintenance grants.

Work, rights and incomes
- A Real Living Wage of at least £10 for all 16+; ban zero-hours contracts; day‑one rights; sectoral collective bargaining; strengthen unions; tackle pay gaps and harassment.
- Reduce average full-time hours to 32 a week within a decade with no loss of pay, driven by productivity gains; enforce rights via a new Workers’ Protection Agency.

Homes and communities
- Build over one million new council and social homes in a decade; end Right to Buy for social housing; zero‑carbon standards; fire safety upgrade fund.
- Rent controls linked to inflation, open‑ended tenancies, national licensing; end rough sleeping in five years.
- Free full‑fibre broadband for all via a publicly owned British Broadband; Post Bank in every community; revive high streets.

Justice, safety and democracy
- Restore neighbourhood policing; public health approach to crime; rehabilitative justice; reunify probation public; restore legal aid; tackle violence against women and girls.
- Final say on Brexit within six months—choice between a credible, jobs‑first customs union deal with single market alignment or remain—and implement the result.
- Clean up politics: abolish the Lords for an elected Senate of the Nations and Regions; expand the franchise to 16; automatic voter registration; curb dark money and lobbying.

A new internationalism
- Put peace, human rights and climate justice at the core: War Powers Act; suspend arms sales used in abuses; recognise Palestine; rebuild climate diplomacy; keep 0.7% aid with a focus on inequality and public services.

For the many, not the few—this fully costed programme will transform Britain and secure a just, green future.
</text>
